Import into an owned native run

html:
Task Contract Compiler

The compiler is an optional request-understanding step inside the existing run owner. task_contract_compilation_enabled defaults to false when no setting is supplied. The mode is bound to run state so a resumed run keeps its accepted interpretation mode.

Plan collaboration is separate from Task Contract. A Plan task retains the requested compiler preference but suppresses effective compilation, including queued preparation. Implementing an approved plan selects Default collaboration and compiles canonical server-owned plan Markdown instead of the visible “Implement the plan.” instruction. Inline generation, source identity, acceptance and queued preparation all use that same source. The approved plan is never a Task Contract or task-board checklist.

For an accepted source revision, the compiler transforms the current uncompiled human input into a structured task contract: request objective, obligations/constraints, explicit references and terminal-output requirements. Its initial model request contains the compiler persona and canonical current source. When the configured route combines compilation with automatic capability selection, it also receives the selector's routing context and may read retained accepted user input once before submitting the contract. Otherwise, available local-memory helper metadata can accompany the source. These conditional helper inputs do not become the source used by the Integrity Guard. The compiler does not receive the executor's complete history/working set or expanded Parameter Store bindings. Known secrets and optional MODEL_INPUT policy apply at their existing projection boundaries.

flowchart TD Source[Current uncompiled human source] --> Build[Build compiler input] Persona[Compiler persona and route] --> Build Routing[Conditional selection context] --> Build Memory[Otherwise local-memory metadata] --> Build Build --> Projection[Project and admit model input] Projection --> Model[Compiler model] Model --> Result[Completed submission] Source --> Guard[Optional provenance guard] Result --> Guard Guard --> Fence[Source and control acceptance fence] Fence --> Revision[Retained intent revision] Revision --> Executor[Executor context assembly] History[Bounded history and runtime evidence] --> Executor Resources[Resource bindings] --> Executor

With ordinary contract substitution, the execution model receives the contract in place of that user input, together with normal bounded conversation history, resource bindings and execution context. Task-skill context mode retains its own input representation: history_messages and project deliberately bypass that substitution when the task-skill policy is enabled. References such as “the same repository” or an attachment name are preserved for the executor to resolve. Historical user messages remain available even when they repeat the current prompt. An amendment is compiled independently; earlier compiled inputs and completed work remain execution context, with later changes taking precedence. ContextStore owns resource identities and grants. The execution task board remains separate from the user-request contract.

Answers to executor ask_user questions also remain verbatim user messages alongside their compiled revisions. Passwords and other exact execution inputs must survive even when the compiler describes their purpose without copying the value. This uses question and answer positions in the existing journal, including continued and steered replies; it does not classify passwords or create a separate credential store. Optional MODEL_INPUT redaction still applies at the consumer boundary. The compiler must also preserve explicitly supplied authentication literals and must not invent credentials.

The implementation reserves the generating attempt before model transport. It records accepted/valid revisions, clarification, stale revisions, failures and cancellation. Changed input can invalidate a revision. A failed compilation has an explicit failed path; it is not an assurance that execution continues with the raw prompt. Inspect the compiler activity and state before deciding whether to resubmit or clarify.

task_contract_models.py defines the generation schema and optional offline fidelity diagnostics. The compiler acceptance path does not call validate_contract or enforce that model. task_contract_fields.py reads tolerant bookkeeping views without rewriting the saved compiler output. task_contract_projection.py supplies the accepted intent to executor requests while preserving the durable human journal.

Compiler responses may include prose alongside the submission tool call. The transport and compiler discard that assistant text before retaining accepted output; only the submission's JSON object becomes the task contract. Streaming previews likewise show only contract arguments. Exactly one smto__submit_task_contract call with complete JSON arguments and a completed tool response is still required for final acceptance. The combined selector's optional retained-input read exchange can precede that submission; it is not an accepted contract. Text-only responses, multiple calls, malformed JSON and truncated responses remain failures. This tolerance applies only to Task Contract compilation, not other bounded internal tool requests.

Source owners: native/task_contract.py, task_contract_models.py, task_contract_fields.py and the request-lifecycle route group. Compilation does not authorize tools, grant credentials or prove that the requested result has been achieved.

sequenceDiagram participant N as Native run or queued session participant C as Shared compiler participant S as Session state owner participant M as Routed model client N->>C: Ensure intent for current source alt Current source already has accepted intent C-->>N: Reuse revision without another compiler call else New source or explicitly admitted retry C->>C: Freeze route-compatible input, schema and saved policy C->>S: Reserve attempt and save generating state C->>C: Check output ceiling and measured context capacity C->>S: Save transport-started accounting C->>M: Call under compiler output/thinking and phase budget opt Combined selection asks to inspect retained accepted input M-->>C: One permitted selection-context read request C->>C: Resolve and redact retained helper result C->>M: Second call with the retained result end M-->>C: Completed submission or generation failure C->>C: Close preview and check final protocol plus optional integrity C->>S: Accept only current source under human-control fences S-->>C: Committed revision or rejected/stale result C-->>N: Accepted intent, clarification wait or failed/stopped compilation end Note over C,M: No Agent or Gateway operation is authorized by compilation

The model-capacity and routing owner is described in Model decisions and inference admission. Compiler failure can stop this sequence before any transport; a generation failure enters another attempt only when the saved recovery policy and current control boundary permit it.

Native acceptance and publication

NativeCompilationSession adapts the shared compiler, capability selector and preview publisher to an owned run. It delegates pause checks, cancellation-owned calls, source-generation checks, saves and events to the native lifecycle. A completed provider response still has to pass the acceptance boundary; it is not itself a durable accepted revision.

On the RAM path, acceptance captures the previous state, stages candidate changes and defers publication events. The atomic commit rechecks Stop, current decision generation and amendments before saving once. Failure restores the local candidate; successful commit precedes event publication. An event-publication error after that commit does not mean the accepted state rolled back. A source already known to be stale is yielded as such so the compiler can persist its stale outcome.

Standalone SQL holds BEGIN IMMEDIATE and routes session saves into that existing transaction after Stop, amendment and generation checks. It does not use the RAM candidate/event staging mechanism. Cancellation settlement reloads authoritative Stop state before marking the compiler phase cancelled, preventing an old recovery status from being restored accidentally.

sequenceDiagram participant C as Compiler participant A as Native compilation session participant H as RAM run transaction participant O as Event observers C->>A: Begin acceptance of completed output A->>H: Read Stop, amendments and decision generation A->>A: Save previous local state and defer publication events A-->>C: Whether source is still current C->>A: Stage accepted revision or stale outcome and save A->>H: Recheck Stop, generation and newly arrived amendments alt Commit is allowed H->>H: Save copied candidate once H-->>A: Committed state A->>O: Publish deferred observations after commit else Control or state check rejects publication H-->>A: Rejection A->>A: Restore previous local candidate end Note over H,O: A post-commit event error does not undo accepted state

Compiler fixtures separate ordinary acceptance from optional strict schema validation. The control-boundary cases in recovery fixtures inject Stop, amendment, changed source, pause and deadline conditions before another compiler call. Their transport is scripted; they do not execute live workloads.

Queued preparation records and import

The repository also provides an internal prepare_task_contract helper that compiles accepted queued intent without creating an AgentLoop, native run, execution attempt or Gateway operation. It is an explicit server-side helper: the checked-out production queue consumes existing preparations but has no automatic caller that schedules this generation function. This protocol does not mean every queued task is compiled in advance.

The caller supplies a client factory for the accepted task context. Claiming happens before client construction and returns the frozen task to only one caller. Other callers receive the existing record, including an in-progress or failed record, and make no additional model call. Eligible work is an unarchived queued chat task with no execution attempt; unresolved Parameter admission prevents preparation. A task can remain blocked by its predecessor while its intent is prepared, because compilation does not satisfy dependencies or reserve execution capacity.

preparation_identity binds the task/conversation, prompt, submission snapshot, compiler input version and selected accepted policy/model/context fields. Reordering the queue or changing a dependency outcome does not change that identity. An accepted prompt or Parameter snapshot edit invalidates the old preparation and permits a new source revision. The canonical approved-plan source is used consistently for compilation and provenance checks.

Preparation state Meaning
generating One owner reserved this accepted source; partial attempt state and transport accounting may already be saved
ready The compiler produced accepted/valid intent, still subject to execution admission
clarification_required The compiler retained a clarification outcome for later native materialization
failed A bounded compiler/factory failure is durable and can be imported without silently recompiling
stale / cancelled Source ownership changed or work was cancelled; the result cannot authorize current intent
consumed A live request/attempt binding imported the server-owned outcome; the first consuming request remains recorded

Standalone SQL uses the task-store lock and writer transaction. RAM uses the task repository's atomic publication and checks identity again inside every save; an earlier snapshot check is insufficient. Both bound private state to 8 MiB of ASCII-encoded JSON. Deleted rows stay deleted, and cancellation/edit hooks retire current records. Provider transport runs outside the SQL acceptance transaction. Normal compiler attempts, recovery budgets and cancellation checks remain with the shared compiler.

A process interruption after transport reservation leaves an ambiguous generating record. Calling the helper again reuses that record instead of resending the request. An existing unusable preparation blocks ordinary execution reservation. The helper does not add a background recovery retry or choose a substitute model when its client factory fails. A plain client must match the accepted model; a routing client retains its existing model-router responsibility.

At native start, native_flow.py consumes a preparation through the authoritative request, current task, lane and attempt binding. Import checks exact conversation/prompt, accepted identity, model, policy, context manifest and saved compiler provenance. A payload-supplied task ID or snapshot does not replace that binding. Repeating consumption for the same request returns a detached snapshot; an explicit retry may reuse an accepted/valid parent result while preserving its original accounting. Restart between consumption and native installation rereads that same result. If no preparation exists, normal on-demand compilation remains available; a corrupt existing record fails validation.

Owner Responsibility
preparation_models.py Private lifecycle/provenance record and accepted-source identity
preparations.py Standalone SQL claims/saves/consumption and shared import validation
memory_preparations.py Current-source checks and atomic RAM publication
preparation_compiler.py Explicit generation session, client factory, budget and safe issue checkpoints
flowchart TD A[Accepted queued intent] --> B[Atomic preparation claim] B --> C[Shared compiler and supplied client] C --> D[Source-checked saved outcome] D --> E[Task admission and attempt binding] E --> F[Validated preparation consumption] F --> G[Owned native installation]

SQL protocol fixtures and RAM fixtures cover single-owner generation, stale replies, provenance, consumption and crash windows with scripted transport. They distinguish compilation evidence from permission to perform task work.

Claiming generation without starting execution

sequenceDiagram participant I as Explicit internal caller participant Q as Preparation helper participant T as Task repository participant F as Accepted-context client factory participant C as Shared compiler I->>Q: Prepare task ID Q->>T: Atomically claim current queued source T->>T: Require eligible unstarted chat and resolved parameter admission alt Compilation disabled T-->>Q: No preparation and no generation owner else Matching record already exists T-->>Q: Existing record without a frozen task for generation else New accepted source T->>T: Retire changed source and reserve generating revision T-->>Q: Preparation plus detached accepted task Q->>F: Construct client from copied accepted context F-->>Q: Client or construction failure Q->>C: Compile through queued session when client is usable C->>T: Source-checked attempt and outcome saves Q->>T: Final save and retained record lookup end Q-->>I: Existing or newly settled preparation Note over I,C: This helper has no automatic production scheduler caller Note over T,C: Queue dependencies and execution capacity remain separate

Only the caller receiving the frozen task constructs a client. Existing matching records, including generating and failed, are returned without another model call. A factory exception is retained as a failed preparation with zero transport calls. The ordinary shared compiler still owns bounded generation recovery when transport begins. A ready result does not release a predecessor, create an attempt or satisfy execution permission.

Changes while generation is in flight

flowchart TD Response[Compiler checkpoint or reply] --> Bound{Within size bound?} Bound -->|No| Reject[Reject publication] Bound -->|Yes| Exists{Record exists?} Exists -->|No| Deleted[Leave deleted intent absent] Exists -->|Yes| Current{Source still current?} Current -->|No| Old[Retain stale or cancelled ownership] Current -->|Yes| Finished{Final save?} Finished -->|No| Partial[Save generating progress] Finished -->|Yes| Outcome[Map compiler outcome] Outcome --> Checkpoint[Publish qualifying runtime issue] Partial --> Stored[Retained source revision] Old --> Stored Checkpoint --> Stored

RAM checks source ownership again inside every save transaction, even if the session just checked it through a read view. SQL performs the equivalent check under its writer transaction. An edit invalidates the old current preparation; removal or queue clearing cancels it through task lifecycle hooks. Late evidence may remain attached to that old record, but cannot become current accepted intent. Deleting the task and preparation prevents a late save from recreating either. Queue reordering alone leaves the accepted-source identity unchanged.

Import into an owned native run

sequenceDiagram participant Q as Task admission participant T as Task store participant N as Native owner participant V as Import validator Q->>T: Check readiness and reserve attempt T-->>Q: Stable request, attempt and lane Q->>N: Start or recover that request N->>N: Strip supplied snapshot and acquire ownership N->>T: Consume by request, conversation and prompt T->>T: Check live task, lane and attempt binding alt No preparation T-->>N: No imported result N->>N: Compile on demand when enabled else Current preparation exists T->>V: Check source, policy, outcome and provenance alt Valid snapshot and consumption lineage V-->>T: Detached allowlisted snapshot T->>T: Record first consumer if absent T-->>N: Retained outcome N->>N: Stage and install under run ownership Note over N: Accepted intent, clarification or failure else Invalid snapshot or lineage V-->>T: Preparation conflict T-->>N: Fail without replacement compilation end end Note over T,N: Recovery before installation rereads the consumed result

The native entry strips client-supplied snapshots and Context manifests before resolving server-owned task state. Consumption is committed before native installation, so its first-consumer record can exist while the initial native checkpoint has no compiler outcome. The recovery branch detects that condition and rereads the preparation instead of issuing another compilation.

Import checks are deliberately stricter than a ready display status:

Check Required retained evidence
Ownership Current running chat task, matching lane/request/attempt and exact conversation/prompt
Source Accepted identity digest and canonical source digest still match the task
Outcome Consumable preparation state, allowlisted snapshot fields and bounded serialized size
Accounting Nonnegative counts, with transport-started attempt count equal to task_contract_calls
Provenance Attempt/revision source digests, compiler model and saved prompt revision match the preparation
Policy Captured compiler policy, guard choice, source count and Context manifest remain consistent
Replay First consumer, the same request, or a qualifying retry whose parent is that first consumer and whose saved contract is accepted/valid

These checks are in validate_preparation_import and validate_snapshot. A routing-aware client factory does not waive the model or accounting checks; an inconsistent existing result fails import rather than silently recompiling. The first consumer remains recorded when an allowed explicit retry reuses its result. Portable snapshots retain compiler intent and accounting, not arbitrary native execution state, resource grants or a permission decision.

Task Contract Integrity Guard

Compiler acceptance remains permissive: validate_contract() stays an optional offline diagnostic and TaskContract.model_validate() is not called during acceptance. Accepted revisions retain schema_validation = "skipped". The separate, deterministic Integrity Guard checks only provenance-sensitive authority before installing a complete, consumer-projected compiler result. It does not inspect streaming fragments, repair output, or invoke a model.

Settings → Task Contracts → Task Contract Integrity Guard defaults ON for new tasks. Task Contract Compilation retains its existing OFF default; the guard has no effect when compilation is disabled. Desktop Prompt Options and mobile Agent options provide an independent override for the next task. “Inherited from Settings” uses the server's current default at admission; “Overridden for this prompt” sends an explicit boolean. Changing the prompt toggle does not write Settings. “Use Settings default” removes the override. Disabling compilation temporarily preserves the prompt choice.

The server freezes the effective boolean task_contract_integrity_guard_enabled when a request is prepared or a task/schedule is admitted. Prepared requests use a separate native_prepared_task_contract_integrity snapshot. Durable queued tasks, scheduled occurrences, resume, restart, continuation and manual compiler retry retain the saved choice. Later Settings changes and draft edits cannot alter it. Current native resume requires the saved guard key; it does not substitute a global default when the key is missing. The portable retry-snapshot adapter has an explicit historical fallback to OFF, distinct from accepting an incomplete current native state. Prompt drafts are scoped by conversation and cleared after successful submission, following existing option lifecycle. Guard OFF preserves historical permissive acceptance.

The guard applies these narrow rules:

  • Explicit source @parameter tokens must appear with the same spelling in generated string leaves; generated parameter tokens must have source provenance. The shared mention lexer excludes emails, escaped mentions, code literals and reserved resource namespaces. No Parameter Store bindings or private values are loaded or compared.
  • High-risk paths are inspected only in scope.roots and scope.targets, including recognizable serialized structures. POSIX absolute paths, Windows drive paths, UNC, file:// URIs, home-rooted paths and traversal segments require explicit source paths. Ordinary relative filenames and paths in descriptive fields remain unrestricted by this guard.
  • Exact explicit paths pass. POSIX, drive and UNC roots also permit syntactic descendants with segment boundaries. Traversal requires the exact source spelling; it never creates descendant authority. Windows separators may be normalized, but case is preserved.

Only the accepted current compiler source establishes provenance, including for amendments. A guessed concrete path fails even if it happens to match a hidden Parameter Store binding. There is no filesystem lookup, Git query, network access, schema/fidelity check, coverage check, graph validation or semantic judgment. Passing is not runtime authorization or complete sandboxing; existing execution permission and containment checks still apply.

Rejected attempts display Integrity check failed, retain bounded findings with optional ACTIVITY projection and start no execution for that revision. They never enter automatic Task Contract recovery, even when recovery is enabled. Retry contract generation remains an explicit user operation and reruns the guard with the captured mode and frozen input. A new task can choose a different setting. Passed, failed and skipped integrity metadata is separate from schema-validation metadata.

V1 uses conservative tokenization rather than shell parsing. Quoted source paths can contain spaces; environment variables, shell substitutions, symlinks, home expansion and URI decoding are not provenance sources. Home and file URI forms require exact matches. The scan bounds nodes (16,384), text (524,288 characters per scan), source candidates (512), findings (32) and diagnostic strings (256 characters). Scope is scanned before unrelated extensions. Excess extension data does not itself reject a contract; partial scans report scan_complete = false and do not claim an unobserved reference was omitted. Protected violations already found still fail. This is a narrow provenance check, not complete contract validation.

flowchart TD Complete[Complete consumer-projected submission] --> Mode{Captured integrity guard enabled?} Mode -->|No| Skip[Record skipped integrity metadata] Mode -->|Yes| Scan[Bounded scan of explicit source and generated references] Scan --> Paths[Check high-risk scope paths against source spellings] Paths --> Mentions[Check parameter-token preservation and provenance] Mentions --> Findings{Violation or internal guard failure?} Findings -->|Yes| Fail[Terminal compiler failure without automatic recovery] Findings -->|No| Pass[Record findings and scan completeness] Skip --> Fence[Normal source and control acceptance fence] Pass --> Fence Fence --> Intent[Accepted intent or clarification] Intent --> Permission[Execution still requires normal authority and receipts]

Output allowance and automatic recovery

Settings → Task Contracts owns the existing compilation toggle and these runtime controls:

Key Default Explicit bounds Meaning
task_contract_max_tokens General ceiling, clamped to 1,024–8,192; zero resolves to 4,096 1,024–65,536 Initial compiler output allowance
task_contract_auto_recovery_enabled Off Boolean Retry failed contract-generation attempts
task_contract_auto_recovery_retries 3 3–10 Additional attempts after the initial call
task_contract_auto_recovery_increment_tokens 1,024 256–8,192, multiples of 256 Linear increase per retry

These controls set model output allowance, not input context, schema size, character limits, or the thinking-token budget. Unsaved installations preserve their old effective allowance within the derived range: a 4,096 global ceiling derives 4,096; a 16,384 ceiling derives 8,192. A ceiling below 1,024 derives a 1,024 compiler allowance and can therefore fail the later output-capacity check. The zero sentinel resolves to the product's 4,096 default. Recovery stays off until explicitly enabled.

The settings owner validates the complete policy under its runtime-control lock and persists one coupled patch in the existing settings namespace. Required headroom is base + retries * increment when recovery is enabled, otherwise base. Saving policy changes raises llm_max_tokens to at least this value, without lowering a larger value. A direct conflicting legacy llm_max_tokens API reduction returns HTTP 422; sequences exceeding 65,536 are rejected. Autosave reconciles server-derived compiler values; the internal ceiling is not a separate Model Configuration editor.

Settings apply to new tasks. Admission, prepared requests, queued tasks and scheduled execution capture the complete output policy and general ceiling together. Native run state and resume context preserve the accepted policy through restarts and continuations. The current snapshot path requires every compiler output/recovery/thinking key in an existing run's state or resume context. An incomplete current snapshot fails with the missing-current-policy diagnostic; new-task default derivation must not be mistaken for an old-run repair mechanism.

The llm_max_tokens ceiling above is the internal client allowance retained for compiler/recovery compatibility. Model Configuration separately controls optional max_completion_tokens for normal agent execution. Saving compiler headroom does not create that execution override, and changing the execution limit, sampling or thinking controls does not change compiler policy. Provider Default may omit the execution limit while reserving internal output space.

Each generation cycle retains a source digest and route-compatible compiler messages, prompt revision and tool schema. Retryable failed generation attempts admit automatic recovery, including wrong tool calls, malformed JSON, incomplete responses, provider/transport errors and output truncation. Retry n requests base + n * increment tokens. For example, 4,096 → 5,120 → 6,144 → 7,168 is one initial call and three additional retries. For an unchanged route, retries reuse captured messages/schema and saved thinking policy. The configured task_contract_retry route can select another role; a role or combined-selection change rebuilds the corresponding prompt/schema. Routing fallback may also rebuild for Main under the router's existing rules, including an admitted preflight-capacity fallback before transport. Every generation failure counts against the same retry limit; changing failure types does not reset it. Clarification, cancellations, stale sources and local failures before generation (such as unavailable input or insufficient context/output capacity) do not start or extend recovery. Integrity violations and internal guard failures also never start automatic recovery.

The request-local task_contract_output_budget ContextVar supplies generation limits; the shared client is never mutated. Preflight reserves the same phase-specific output allowance sent in the provider payload. That reservation participates in cache identity and working-set sizing, including existing constrained Agent recovery. If compiler input plus the next allowance cannot fit the model context window, recovery stops before the provider call. Provider output ceilings may be lower than the public setting maximum; provider rejection is retried within the saved retry limit and retained with its original reason.

Every compiler call has a durable reserved attempt before transport. Attempts retain revision identity, attempt identity, retry index, configured and effective limits, completion state and bounded visible failure evidence. A preflight-rejected allowance is recorded with transport_started=false and does not increment task_contract_calls. Retries are attempts of the same contract revision, not new semantic revisions. task_contract.attempt_failed is nonterminal; task_contract.recovery_started and the next task_contract.started show progress and limits. Only terminal failure emits task_contract.failed. Accepted and failed attempts remain inspectable on desktop/mobile.

Each transport contributes to task_contract_calls, total model calls and accumulated Task Contract usage. Each compiler attempt gets a separate two-call phase budget; ordinary compilation uses one call, while combined selection can read retained accepted input and use the second call for final submission. Executor decision allowance remains untouched. No Agent or Gateway tool execution starts until a contract is accepted. Failed partial output remains bounded and sanitized; private provider reasoning is excluded and raw compiler input is not copied into attempt records.

Between retries the owner checks cancellation, amendments/source digest, pause and wall budget. An interrupted generating or recovery_pending checkpoint fails conservatively as interrupted_compilation on re-entry; it never invisibly resends a provider request. This also applies when paused between attempts. The existing Retry contract generation control explicitly reopens the same accepted task, retaining its frozen input and saved policy. Frozen input is reused only when its input version, source digest and route identity match. Otherwise explicit retry rebuilds it from the saved current source and current compiler input rules, including conditional routing/memory helper context. Each manual admission starts one fresh, bounded recovery cycle. Settings edits do not alter that saved cycle; submit a new task to use a changed policy.

flowchart TD Enter[Enter current-source compiler] --> Pending{Unsettled generation checkpoint?} Pending -->|Yes| Interrupted[Fail interrupted without resend] Pending -->|No| Attempt[Reserve attempt and allowance] Attempt --> Capacity{Capacity fits?} Capacity -->|No| Route[Configured preflight fallback] Route --> Fits{Fallback fits?} Fits -->|No| Failed[Retain terminal failure] Fits -->|Yes| Transport[Start compiler transport] Capacity -->|Yes| Transport Transport --> Result{Attempt result} Result -->|Accepted or clarification| Retain[Retain revision and outcome] Result -->|Cancelled or stale| Stop[Settle control or source outcome] Result -->|Failure| Retry{Recovery eligible?} Retry -->|No| Failed Retry -->|Yes| Save[Save recovery-pending and failure] Save --> Boundary[Recheck controls, source and budget] Boundary --> Allowed{Another attempt allowed?} Allowed -->|No| Stop Allowed -->|Yes| Next[Select retry route and allowance] Next --> Attempt Failed -.-> Manual[Explicit source-bound retry admission]

Recovery eligibility requires a retryable failure, started transport, enabled saved recovery and remaining retries. This diagram starts after enabled/current-intent checks. An already failed compiler returns its retained failure until explicit retry admission reopens it; an unchanged accepted contract returns without a call. Manual admission also checks Stop, tombstones and newer amendments before renewing the same task's wall budget.

Thinking during Task Contract generation

Settings → Task Contracts also exposes task_contract_thinking_mode and task_contract_thinking_budget_tokens. They apply only to compilation, including its automatic retries. They do not change the agent's subsequent decisions, responses or general recovery configuration, or other tasks using the same client.

Normal execution has its own Thinking control in Model Configuration. Both use chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking for an explicit On/Off choice, but the execution override never replaces the compiler's saved thinking policy. For example, execution Thinking Off and Task Contract thinking On send false for normal decisions and true for contract generation, including its retries. Their thinking budgets are also independent, even when calls share the same model client.

Mode Provider request
Provider default No thinking override
Off (disabled, default for new tasks) chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking=false
On (enabled) chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking=true
Bounded budget (budget) Thinking enabled, plus thinking_token_budget

The explicit modes require an endpoint that supports those controls. Capability support is not inferred from model names, aliases or provider branding. A rejected control is reported as a provider failure; the runtime never silently retries without the policy. The general llm_recovery_thinking=auto compatibility setting now means provider defaults for every model. Existing explicitly configured general budget, disabled and unchanged modes retain their behavior.

The thinking budget defaults to 1,024, accepts 128–32,768 in increments of 128, and is used only in Bounded budget mode. In that mode it must be smaller than the initial Task Contract output allowance. Retries increase the output allowance as before and leave the thinking budget fixed. With a reasoning model, hidden thinking can consume the output allowance before any contract text or tool call appears; raising the output limit is not the only remedy.

Thinking policy is snapshotted alongside output policy at admission, including queued, prepared and scheduled tasks, and survives manual retries, restart and continuation. Current saved tasks require complete thinking policy; missing keys are not silently replaced with Provider default. The request-local task_contract_thinking ContextVar is set for the compiler call and reset in finally on success, failure, cancellation or interruption. The shared client and global settings are never modified. Attempt inspection and history retain the selected policy.

Failure messages identify exhausted retries and recovery stopped before exhaustion. Output-limit messages also distinguish disabled recovery. These messages derive recovery status from the saved attempt's policy. They never assume that recovery is disabled when older metadata is missing. No-visible-output failures also suggest reviewing thinking settings instead of repeatedly increasing the output limit.

Streaming compiler output

Native Task Contract calls request SSE streaming when the endpoint supports it. The existing activity inspector on desktop and mobile refreshes Generated output (partial) while the compiler is still running. Previews expose completed JSON values and nested container members; unfinished strings are withheld until complete structured projection is possible. Private reasoning and provider extensions are never shown. The complete response must still pass the existing protocol checks before contract acceptance or any execution.

Sanitized previews are bounded to 192 KiB and checkpointed at most twice per second. task_contract.progress carries only attempt identity and a monotonically increasing detail_version. An open inspector fetches the latest checkpoint without polling or closing the disclosure; a closed inspector makes no preview requests. Reconnects use the retained checkpoint and never start another inference. Terminal events replace the preview with the accepted contract or retained failure evidence. Older or late progress cannot overwrite a newer checkpoint or a terminal attempt. Cancellation closes the publisher before state is finalized, and each retry keeps its own preview and identity.

A confirmed streaming rejection before an SSE response opens may fall back to the existing single-response transport with exactly the same output/thinking policy. An interrupted or malformed open stream never triggers an invisible resend. Output-limit recovery remains unchanged. Streaming improves visibility and time to first visible contract content; it does not reduce the requested output budget or guarantee faster model generation.

sequenceDiagram participant T as Compiler transport participant P as Contract preview publisher participant S as Saved attempt participant U as Activity inspector T->>P: Partial tool-call argument fragments P->>P: Check open/current/generating state and throttle interval P->>P: Require one contract call within byte limit P->>P: Parse complete values and project safe fields opt Safe preview changed P->>S: Save preview with increasing sequence P-->>U: Progress invalidation and attempt identity U->>S: Fetch retained detail when inspector is open S-->>U: Latest safe checkpoint end T->>P: Close before final acceptance or failure settlement Note over P,S: Later callbacks cannot replace terminal or closed output Note over T,U: Preview text never authorizes execution or bypasses final validation

The preview owner is task_contract_stream.py; attempt output and explicit retry admission live in task_contract_attempts.py. The schema/provenance distinction and runtime policy remain independent of how quickly a preview reaches the inspector.
